episodes.title: Morning Orders
episodes.text: You arrive in the small office and sit down by the radio. You pick up the handset and listen. You copy down today's route, timetable, and cargoes from the dispatcher.

episodes.title: Talking Through the Run
episodes.text: You stand beside the engine with the engineer before departure. You go over the route and timetable together.

choice.prompt: The engineer asks if you want to double-check one part of the plan now. What do you go over again?

options.label: Go over the cargo and timetable again
options.outcome: You read the cargo and times back together and both nod. You board knowing you agree on the plan.

options.label: Skip the check and start moving
options.outcome: You wave it off and climb aboard. You start the day unsure you heard the times the same way.

chat.text: Morning. What did dispatch give us for route and cargo today?
Any word on defects or slow spots on that stretch?
Okay, so we are clear on the plan before I start up?

episodes.title: Giving the Go
episodes.text: You stand where the engineer can see you. You raise your hand signal and speak into the radio. You watch as the train begins to roll.

episodes.title: Watching the Monitor
episodes.text: You sit by the screen and listen for dispatcher updates. Nothing new comes in about train or rail problems. It is the same watch as yesterday, and the same again tomorrow.

episodes.title: Stopped on the Track
episodes.text: The train jerks to an emergency stop on open track. You get out and see you will need warning out. You turn to the nearby workers to get signals placed.

choice.prompt: You must tell the workers where to set warning signals. What do you order?

options.label: Set warning signals in front and at rear
options.outcome: The workers walk both ways with flags and lights. Approaching trains can see you are stopped from either direction.

options.label: Set a warning only in front
options.outcome: One worker goes ahead with a signal while the rear stays dark. Trains coming from behind have no warning of your stop.

options.label: Wait and set no warnings yet
options.outcome: Everyone stands by the stopped train. No protection goes up in front or behind while you wait.

episodes.title: Finding Another Way
episodes.text: You sit with the engineer after the stop is cleared. You talk through the rail defect ahead. You discuss another route that keeps your timetable and cargo safe.

trial.title: Spot the Problem First
trial.scenario: The dispatcher radios about a rail defect ahead. Your monitor also shows a problem on the same stretch. The engineer waits to hear about the route.
options: Tell the engineer about the defect and discuss another route
Signal the engineer to go faster through the defect
Keep the same route and ignore the warning
trial.explain: A defect means you confer with the engineer about another route.

episodes.title: Checking Your Headset
episodes.text: You arrive at your desk and log in from home. You put on your headset and open the electronic listening system. You listen to the speaker's test statements to catch the meaning before anyone needs you.

trial.title: Listen First
trial.scenario: You are listening through your electronic system before translating. The speaker is talking fast and one phrase is unclear. You need to get the meaning right before you speak.
options: Start translating right away and guess the unclear phrase
Ask for the unclear part to be repeated so you understand it
Turn off the listening system and work without it
trial.explain: You listen first to determine meaning before you prepare the translation.

episodes.title: Translating The Meeting
episodes.text: You join an online meeting and translate consecutively after each speaker pauses. You keep the content, context, and style as close as you can. You switch back and forth between the two languages as people talk.

episodes.title: Building Word Lists
episodes.text: You sit with your notes and compile terminology for this week's jobs. You look up the exact technical terms for a medical form. You save them in your list to use in translations.

episodes.title: Same List Again
episodes.text: You go back through the same terminology list as yesterday. You check each entry and fix small typos. Tomorrow you will do the same list again.

episodes.title: Words For Students
episodes.text: You meet online with a teacher to go over material for students.

choice.prompt: The teacher waits for you to decide how to adapt the translation for the students' level.

options.label: Simplify the wording together now
options.outcome: You rewrite the sentences together in simpler words and the teacher approves them for class.

options.label: Keep the wording as it is
options.outcome: You leave the text unchanged and the teacher sets it aside to review later.

chat.text: These paragraphs are too advanced for this grade level.
Can we adapt the translation to match their reading level?

episodes.title: Asked To Share
episodes.text: You are translating a private call and hear confidential information. Afterward someone asks you to repeat what was said. You remember the ethical code that protects confidentiality.

choice.prompt: The person presses you to share the confidential information from the session.

options.label: Refuse and protect the information
options.outcome: You say you cannot share it and you keep the information private.

options.label: Share a small part of it
options.outcome: You pass on a detail and break the confidentiality rule for the job.

options.label: Tell them to ask the speaker directly
options.outcome: You point them to the speaker and you do not disclose anything yourself.

episodes.title: Watching the Loading
episodes.text: You arrive at the dock as the crew starts loading. You stand back where you can see the whole bay. You watch to make sure they follow the loading procedures.

episodes.title: Checking the Bracing
episodes.text: You climb into the trailer to inspect the loaded freight. You push against the bracing and blocking with your hand. You look down each row to check that nothing can shift.

trial.title: Find the loose load
trial.scenario: You are checking a finished load. Two pallets are tight with solid blocking. One heavy drum has a gap behind the brace and can rock when you push it.
options: The heavy drum with the gap and movement
The tight pallet on the left
The tight pallet on the right
trial.explain: The loose heavy drum is the one that is not securely braced.

episodes.title: Showing Heavy Stow
episodes.text: You stop the crew before they stow the heavy barrels. You show them how to place them for this load.

choice.prompt: The crew wants to stack the heavy barrels high to save space. What do you tell them?

options.label: Put them low and show blocking
options.outcome: You show them how to stow the barrels low and blocked. They reset the load and it holds steady.

options.label: Let them stack them high
options.outcome: They stack the barrels high. The load feels top-heavy and you have to stop work to fix it.

chat.text: These barrels are heavy. Where do you want them?
Can we just stack them on top to save space?

episodes.title: Writing Down Details
episodes.text: You sit with your notebook and write down freight conditions and handling. You note the same kinds of details as yesterday. You know you will do the same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Load Shifts Loose
episodes.text: You see a pallet has shifted and the blocking has slipped. You stop the crew from adding more freight. You stand by the open bay looking at the loose brace.

choice.prompt: The brace is loose and the crew is waiting. What do you do first?

options.label: Stop loading and re-brace now
options.outcome: You hold the loading until the freight is braced again. The crew resets the blocking and you check it.

options.label: Keep loading around it
options.outcome: You let them keep loading. The shifted pallet presses on the next freight and the problem gets worse.

options.label: Record it and walk away
options.outcome: You write it down and leave the bay. The loose freight stays unsecured on the trailer.

episodes.title: Filing the Report
episodes.text: You sit down after the shipment is complete. You prepare your report on the freight and the problems you saw. You submit it and close the file for the day.

episodes.title: Morning One To One
episodes.text: You arrive and set out two chairs at the small table. You sit down with your first student for private instruction. You walk through yesterday's math problems together at a slow pace.

episodes.title: Nervous Before Test
episodes.text: You sit down with a student who has a test tomorrow. She looks tired and says she will probably fail. You pause the review to give her some steady feedback.

choice.prompt: She is shutting down. How do you respond right now?

options.label: Point out what she got right
options.outcome: She nods and keeps working. You finish the worksheet together.

options.label: Push her to do more problems
options.outcome: She does the next set quietly. It takes longer and she stays tense.

episodes.title: Same Worksheets Again
episodes.text: You sit with the next student and open the same worksheet set. You go over the answers line by line. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Study Skills Practice
episodes.text: You sit with a small group at the back table. You show them how to take short notes while they read. Then you have them try it on the next page.

trial.title: Encourage a stuck student
trial.says: I keep messing this up. I am just bad at this.
options: You are getting the first steps right, let's keep going together.
You need to try harder if you want to pass.
Maybe this subject just is not for you.
trial.explain: Positive reinforcement keeps confidence up while you keep teaching.

episodes.title: Stuck On Problems
episodes.text: You are reviewing solutions when a student stops and will not continue. His work shows he has lost track of the steps. You need to decide how to get him moving again.

choice.prompt: He is stuck and frustrated. What do you do next?

options.label: Go back and rework one problem slowly
options.outcome: He follows along and finishes the step. You move on to the next problem together.

options.label: Switch to test-taking tips for a bit
options.outcome: He listens and takes a breath. You return to the problem after a short break.

options.label: Check his progress and end early
options.outcome: You note where he stopped. He packs up and leaves for the day.

episodes.title: Checking Today's Progress
episodes.text: You sit alone and look back over today's worksheets and notes. You mark what each student finished and where they struggled. You stack the folders for tomorrow.

episodes.title: The core work
episodes.text: You start the main work of a UGC Creator — the core of the job, done properly, start to finish. No audience and no shortcut: this is the thing everything else in the day supports. This is the work the whole job is built around.

episodes.title: People time
episodes.text: People need things from you — questions, help, decisions. You deal with them one at a time, the way this job always does. Real people, real reactions — this is the human side of the job, as it actually feels.

choice.prompt: Someone you're working with asks you to take on one more thing — extra work, on top of everything already in front of you today.

options.label: Say yes and fit it in
options.outcome: You fit it in. The day runs longer, the work gets done properly — and the person who asked remembers that you said yes.

options.label: Say no, politely
options.outcome: You say no, and you say why. A short, slightly awkward moment — then the rest of your day stays yours.

options.label: Offer a smaller version
options.outcome: You offer the part you can actually do, and by when. Most days that's accepted — saying yes to everything is how this job burns people out.

episodes.title: Hands on
episodes.text: Tools-and-systems time: you work the equipment and the screens of the trade until the thing in front of you does what it should. Skilled, hands-on work — the part where being good at it shows.

trial.title: The check-in
trial.says: Hey — how's that thing coming along that you were working on?
options: It's on track. I'll flag it straight away if I need help or it slips.
Fine.
Honestly? Don't ask. It's a disaster.
trial.explain: The professional reply says where things stand and what happens next — short, honest, no drama.

episodes.title: The routine block
episodes.text: The same block as yesterday: the repeating tasks that never make the brochure. You do them again, carefully, because skipping them is exactly how mistakes happen. The same again tomorrow. This block repeats more than any other part of the job.

episodes.title: It goes wrong
episodes.text: Something goes wrong — it always does, some days. A problem lands on you that was in nobody's plan, and sorting it out is now your job. Unplanned and unavoidable — how the job feels when it pushes back.

episodes.title: The paperwork
episodes.text: End of day: notes, records, the write-up of everything you did. The work isn't finished until it's written down. Nobody's favourite part. It still has to be done, every day.

episodes.title: Layering Density Maps
episodes.text: You arrive and set your coffee down. You sit down and open the land area base map. You pull up population density and start layering it over the blocks.

trial.title: Build the land use report
items: Write the short narrative summary
Prepare the final report package
Gather the land area base map
Overlay the population density data
trial.explain: You start with the base map, add the data, then write it up.

episodes.title: Feasibility Memo Draft
episodes.text: You sit down with the housing proposal file. You check costs, rules, and fit with current zoning. You type a short note for the planning officials on what will work.

episodes.title: Working the Zoning Draft
episodes.text: You sit at the table with the draft land use plan. You walk through setbacks, utilities, and road space. You mark where the housing language needs to change.

choice.prompt: The draft allows more homes but strains the bus line. Do you keep it or pull it back?

options.label: Keep the housing and note the bus fix
options.outcome: You keep the housing level and add a note about bus capacity. The officials read it and ask for cost options.

options.label: Pull housing back to fit transit
options.outcome: You lower the housing numbers to match the current bus line. The draft moves forward with fewer changes needed.

episodes.title: Updating the Same Files
episodes.text: You sit back down after lunch. You open the same tracking sheet as yesterday. You copy in today's parcel numbers. Same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Listening at City Hall
episodes.text: You sit at the front table in the meeting room. Residents and a developer fill the chairs to talk about the community plan.

chat.text: Will this plan take our parking for bike lanes?
We have the draft map here if you want to point to your block.
Our street floods now. What about drains first?

episodes.title: Neighbors Disagree Hard
episodes.text: You stay after the meeting with two groups still arguing. You sit down between them with the alternative site sketch. Voices stay sharp about the community facility location.

choice.prompt: Both sides want an answer now. How do you step in?

options.label: Pause and walk through the alternative sketch
options.outcome: You lay out the second site and talk through access and noise. They agree to look at it before next week.

options.label: End for today and set a follow-up
options.outcome: You close the talk and set a time to meet again. Everyone leaves tired but calmer.

options.label: Ask each side to state one need
options.outcome: Each person names one clear need for the facility. You write them down to shape the next draft.

episodes.title: The core work
episodes.text: You start the main work of a UX Researcher — the core of the job, done properly, start to finish. No audience and no shortcut: this is the thing everything else in the day supports. This is the work the whole job is built around.

episodes.title: Loading the Morning Van
episodes.text: You arrive at your small storage space. You count boxes of snacks and drinks onto your cart. You pack coins, small bills, and extra supplies for the day.

episodes.title: Checking Each Machine
episodes.text: You walk the same row you walked yesterday. You press each button and watch it vend to test it. You see the same lights and hear the same hum, same as tomorrow.

episodes.title: Collecting and Settling Up
episodes.text: You kneel by the lobby machine with your money bag. You pull the cash box while the manager watches.

choice.prompt: The cash in the box is a few dollars short of what the invoice should show. What do you do?

options.label: Count it again with him there
options.outcome: You count the bills and coins again together. You both see the same total and you write that down.

options.label: Write down what you found
options.outcome: You finish the invoice for the cash you have. You note the short amount to check next visit.

chat.text: How much was in there today?
Can you make me an invoice before you go?
We need to settle up for this week.

episodes.title: Jammed Bill Acceptor
episodes.text: You find a note taped to the drink machine saying bills won't go in. You open the front and look at the bill slot. You see a crumpled bill jammed tight inside.

choice.prompt: The bill is stuck fast and people are waiting to use the machine. What do you do?

options.label: Clear the jammed bill now
options.outcome: You pull the crumpled bill out carefully. You run a test bill through to see it take money again.

options.label: Leave it and come back later
options.outcome: You close the machine and leave an out-of-order note. You lose those sales until you return.

episodes.title: Reading Meters Closely
episodes.text: You stand at the snack machine with your list. You read the meter and look at what is left on each row. You check for anything stuck or running low.

trial.title: Find the fault first
trial.scenario: You run a test vend and nothing drops. You look inside and see one bag wedged sideways in the coil. The meter still counts fine.
options: Stuck product blocking the coil
Empty coin tube for change
Dusty glass on the front
trial.explain: The wedged bag stops the drop even when the meter counts.

episodes.title: Counting Cash and Records
episodes.text: You sit down with the day's cash and your notebook. You count the coins and bills from each machine. You write down what you sold and what money you collected.

episodes.title: The core work
episodes.text: You start the main work of a Vertical Farm Technician — the core of the job, done properly, start to finish. No audience and no shortcut: this is the thing everything else in the day supports. This is the work the whole job is built around.

episodes.title: People time
episodes.text: A quiet stretch: mostly you and the work. Human contact in this job is the exception, not the rule — long solo runs are the normal texture of the day. Real people, real reactions — this is the human side of the job, as it actually feels.

choice.prompt: A message lands: could you also take on one more thing today — extra work, on top of everything already in front of you?

options.label: Say yes and fit it in
options.outcome: You fit it in. The day runs longer, the work gets done properly — and the person who asked remembers that you said yes.

options.label: Say no, politely
options.outcome: You say no, and you say why. A short, slightly awkward moment — then the rest of your day stays yours.

options.label: Offer a smaller version

episodes.title: Hands on
episodes.text: Hands-on time. You make, fix or adjust the real thing in front of you — the part of the job you can touch, and the part where skill is visible. Skilled, hands-on work — the part where being good at it shows.

trial.says: Hey — how's that thing coming along that you were working on?
options: It's on track. I'll flag it straight away if I need help or it slips.
Fine.
Honestly? Don't ask. It's a disaster.

episodes.title: Counting Controlled Drugs
episodes.text: You arrive and unlock the drug cabinet. You count each vial against yesterday's list. You write the numbers into the log book.

episodes.title: Running Morning Labs
episodes.text: You sit down with blood, urine, and fecal samples. You run blood counts and urinalyses. You label results to assist with diagnosis.

trial.title: Pick What Needs Attention
trial.scenario: You have three samples on the counter for morning testing. One urine cup has no label, one blood tube is clearly labeled, one fecal cup is labeled and sealed.
options: The unlabeled urine sample
The clearly labeled blood tube
The labeled and sealed fecal cup
trial.explain: A sample without a label cannot be tested for diagnosis.

episodes.title: Vaccines With Vet
episodes.text: You prepare the morning vaccines the veterinarian prescribed.

choice.prompt: The dog tenses as you lift the syringe. What do you do?

options.label: Pause and steady him
options.outcome: You wait, hold him gently, and give the vaccine cleanly. He settles once it is done.

options.label: Give it quickly anyway
options.outcome: You give the shot while he moves. The vet asks you to check for leakage and note it.

chat.text: That one gets the booster today.
Can you draw it up and give it?

episodes.title: Under Anesthesia Watch
episodes.text: You stay beside the dog under anesthesia.

choice.prompt: Her breathing slows and her response changes. What do you do first?

options.label: Alert the vet at once
options.outcome: You call it out right away. She directs you to adjust the dosage while she watches.

options.label: Watch a little longer alone
options.outcome: You keep watching without speaking. Her levels dip further before the vet steps in.

options.label: Adjust dosage yourself
options.outcome: You reach for the dial alone. The vet stops you and gives the direction herself.

chat.text: I need you on monitoring.
Tell me if her response changes.

episodes.title: Same Meds Again
episodes.text: You measure out the afternoon medications. Same doses, same animals, same charting. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Watching Wake Ups
episodes.text: You sit with animals waking up from surgery. You watch their breathing and check them often. You keep them warm and still until they are steady.

episodes.title: First Exam Table
episodes.text: You arrive and wash your hands. You sit down with a coughing dog on the table. You listen to its chest and feel its belly to find what is wrong.

episodes.title: Blood Draws Again
episodes.text: You sit on the same stool and draw blood from cat after cat. You label each tube and set it in the rack. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Ultrasound In Dark
episodes.text: You bring a lab into the dark room. You move the probe over its belly and watch the screen. You read the image for fluid where it should not be.

trial.title: Run the ultrasound scan
items: Read the image for what it shows
Hold the probe still to capture the view
Help the dog stay still on the table
Put gel on the belly for the probe
trial.explain: You settle the animal first, then apply gel before you scan and read.

episodes.title: Shots With Owner
episodes.text: You meet a puppy and its owner for vaccines.

choice.prompt: The puppy hides behind the owner’s legs before its shot. What do you do?

options.label: Give the inoculation quickly now
options.outcome: You give the shot while the owner holds her. She yelps and then sits still for the sticker in her record.

options.label: Let her sniff and settle first
options.outcome: You wait a minute and talk softly while she sniffs your hand. You give the rabies shot and she barely flinches.

chat.text: Is this the rabies shot? Will it hurt her?
She was scared last time at the vet.

episodes.title: Bleeding Leg Wound
episodes.text: You are called in for a dog with a deep cut on its leg. Blood soaks through the towel. You press gauze on it to slow the bleeding.

choice.prompt: The wound is still bleeding under the gauze. What do you do next?

options.label: Clean and dress the wound now
options.outcome: You clean the cut and wrap it tight with fresh dressing. You watch it for ten minutes to check the bleeding stops.

options.label: Take it straight to surgery
options.outcome: You move the dog to the table for surgery to close the cut. You tie off the vessel and stitch the skin shut.

options.label: Collect blood first for testing
options.outcome: You draw blood while keeping pressure on the leg. You send the sample off and return to cleaning the wound.

episodes.title: Setting The Bone
episodes.text: You see a cat with a swollen front leg. You feel the break and line up the bone with your hands. You wrap it firm and prescribe medicine for pain.

episodes.title: Morning Kennels
episodes.text: You arrive to the same row of kennels as yesterday. You scrub bowls, sweep floors, and wipe down the holding areas. The disinfectant smell sits heavy while you work through each cage.

episodes.title: Holding Still
episodes.text: You lift the terrier onto the exam table. You hold him steady around his shoulders while the vet checks his leg. He trembles under your hands and tries to pull away.

choice.prompt: The dog starts twisting hard in your grip. What do you do?

options.label: Tighten your hold and keep him still
options.outcome: You firm up your grip and the vet finishes the check. The dog pants hard and scratches your forearm.

options.label: Pause and let him settle
options.outcome: You loosen up and speak low until he stops shaking. The exam takes a few minutes longer to finish.

episodes.title: Filling Bottles
episodes.text: You sit down at the counter with the morning prescriptions. You count out tablets and pour them into small bottles. You stick on each label and line them up for check.

trial.title: Fill a prescription
items: Set the labeled bottle out for check
Read the prescription label
Put the pills in the bottle and label it
Count out the pills
trial.explain: You read first, then count, bottle, and set out for check.

episodes.title: Surgery Help
episodes.text: You stand by the operating table in scrubs. You help give the anesthetic and watch the monitor for breathing and heart rate. You stay close and adjust as the vet directs.

episodes.title: Waking Up Wrong
episodes.text: You check the recovery cages after surgery. The beagle is breathing fast and feels hot to the touch.

choice.prompt: Her breathing stays fast and uneven. What do you do?

options.label: Call the vet in right away
options.outcome: You call out and the vet comes to the cage at once. She checks the dog and takes over her care.

options.label: Watch five more minutes alone
options.outcome: You stay and watch her breathing on the clock. You call the vet when it does not slow down.

chat.text: How is the beagle in cage two?
Is her breathing still fast?
Tell me her gums and temp and I will come now.

episodes.title: Evening Hold
episodes.text: You walk into the exam room with a nervous cat and her owner. You wrap the cat in a towel and hold her still for the vet. You talk low to keep them both calm.

episodes.title: Watching Yesterday's Footage
episodes.text: You sit down at your desk and open the project. You play the raw clips sequence by sequence. You make small notes so you know what you have before you start cutting.

episodes.title: Notes From Director
episodes.text: You open the script and the director's notes beside your timeline.

choice.prompt: You have a lot of raw footage and the director wants it kept in script order. How do you start?

options.label: Lay the clips down in script order first
options.outcome: You string the footage into a rough continuous whole. It matches the script and is ready to tighten later.

options.label: Cut out your favorite parts first
options.outcome: You pull strong moments aside for now. You still need to put them back into script order afterward.

chat.text: Let's keep this part in the order I wrote it.
String the wide shots together first, then drop in the close parts.

episodes.title: Setting Up Machines
episodes.text: You turn on the editing computer and open the same project. You check the drives and the editing setup. You wait for everything to load, same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Picking Best Shots
episodes.text: You look at three takes of the same scene side by side. You pick the clearest one where the action reads well. You join the chosen shots so the story moves without a jump.

trial.title: Put the scene together
items: Join the chosen shots in story order
Look through all the shots for the scene
Check that the story runs smooth
Pick the shots that work best
trial.explain: You look first, pick second, join third, then check the flow.

episodes.title: Fixing Bad Audio
episodes.text: You play back your sequence and hear a gap where the dialogue drops out. You stop and mark the bad section. You need to fix it now before you can move on.

choice.prompt: The dialogue cuts out in the middle of the sequence. What do you do first?

options.label: Replace the missing dialogue with a clean take
options.outcome: You find the clean line and set it into the gap. The sentence plays whole again.

options.label: Leave the gap and keep arranging
options.outcome: You keep working around the hole. You still have to come back and repair the missing line.

options.label: Ask the director which take to use
options.outcome: You send the two options and wait for an answer. You fix the cut once she picks one.

episodes.title: Adding Music and Titles
episodes.text: You sit back at your editing system for the final pass. You lay in the music and sound effects under the picture. You set up the titling tool and add the opening titles.

episodes.title: Framing Morning Light
episodes.text: You arrive on the set while the lights are still cool. You look through the viewfinder and compose and frame the first shot. You set lenses and filters to get the soft look the director asked for.

trial.title: Set the Shot
items: Dial in camera settings
Compose and frame each shot
Choose film and filters
Set the light and lenses
trial.explain: You frame first, then shape light and glass before you lock the settings.

episodes.title: Checking Focus Again
episodes.text: You sit by the camera and adjust focus and exposure. You check the lighting again and tweak the controls. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Telling Camera Crew
episodes.text: You gather the two camera operators before the next setup.

choice.prompt: Both operators are waiting on your cue to start. How do you call it?

options.label: Give one clear start cue
options.outcome: You call the start once and both cameras roll together. The angles match and you move on.

options.label: Let each operator start on their own
options.outcome: You nod to each one separately. One starts late and you have to reset and shoot it again.

chat.text: Where do you want us for this one?
We need the same start cue on both cameras.

episodes.title: Rolling the Scene
episodes.text: You get behind the camera as the set goes quiet. You operate the camera and record the scene for the broadcast. You hold the frame steady through the whole take.

episodes.title: Losing the Exposure
episodes.text: You are mid-take when a cloud shifts and the light jumps. The picture washes out and focus slips. You keep rolling while you fix the controls.

choice.prompt: The image is too bright and soft. What do you adjust first?

options.label: Stop and reset exposure and focus
options.outcome: You cut the take and reset exposure and focus. You lose a minute but the next take is clean.

options.label: Keep rolling and ride it out
options.outcome: You keep recording with the bright, soft image. The moment passes and the footage stays unusable.

episodes.title: Cutting Today's Footage
episodes.text: You sit down at the edit desk with today's scenes. You open the timeline and trim the clips together. You save a rough cut for broadcast review.

episodes.title: Hello Morning Calls
episodes.text: You sit down at your computer and put on your headset. You greet the first caller and ask how you can help. You listen and direct the call to the right person.

episodes.title: Same Database Entries
episodes.text: You open the database and start entering information. You type row after row, the same as yesterday. You save, close, and know it will be the same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Updating Client Files
episodes.text: You sit with your word processing and database programs open. You create a new file and enter the updated information. You check it once before you save it.

trial.title: Enter database information in order
items: Type the new information into the fields
Check the entries for mistakes
Open the database on your computer
Save the database and close it
trial.explain: You open the file first, then type, check, and save last.

episodes.title: Lines Ring Together
episodes.text: You are at your desk when two calls come in at once and a third is waiting.

choice.prompt: Both lines are ringing and one caller is waiting. What do you do first?

options.label: Answer one caller, take a clear message
options.outcome: You answer the first line and write down the message. The other caller waits a moment longer but you get to them next.

options.label: Try to handle both callers at once
options.outcome: You put one on hold and switch back and forth. You take both messages but you have to ask each caller to repeat details.

options.label: Let them ring and call back later
options.outcome: You let the calls go and check the missed messages. You call each person back and take their information then.

chat.text: Hi, I need to speak to payroll right now, it's urgent.
Hello? Are you still there? I also left a message earlier.

episodes.title: Payroll Timekeeping Check
episodes.text: You open the timekeeping sheet on your computer. You compare the hours and enter the corrections into the payroll file. You submit the updated information for processing.

episodes.title: Visitor Needs Direction
episodes.text: You see a visitor waiting on video and you greet them. They are unsure who they need to see. You ask what their inquiry is about.

choice.prompt: The visitor explains a billing question you cannot answer yourself. What do you do?

options.label: Direct them to the right person
options.outcome: You transfer the call to the billing contact and note the inquiry. They get to speak with someone who can help.

options.label: Take their information and promise a callback
options.outcome: You write down their name and question and pass it on. They wait for a return call later today.

episodes.title: Morning Script Study
episodes.text: You arrive at the small rehearsal room early. You sit down with your script and a coffee. You read your part out loud and mark your cues.

episodes.title: Talking With Director
episodes.text: You sit with the director at the table. She wants to try your role a different way.

choice.prompt: The director asks which reading you want to try next.

options.label: Try the softer reading
options.outcome: You read the lines again softer and slower. She nods and marks it in her script.

options.label: Keep your first reading
options.outcome: You read it the same way again. She listens, then asks you to still try it softer once.

chat.text: That first read was clear. Can we try it softer this time?
Less rush on the second line. Let it land.
What do you think fits him better?

episodes.title: Repeating Your Lines
episodes.text: You stand in the corner and run the same lines again. You say them, pause for the cue, and say them again. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Ensemble Practice Together
episodes.text: You gather with the other actors around the mics. You run the scene together and listen for each other's cues. You adjust your timing to stay with the group.

trial.title: Learn your part in order
items: Learn your lines
Study the script
Interpret the role
Memorize your cues
trial.explain: You study first, then decide how to play it before you lock in lines and cues.

episodes.title: Funny Then Serious
episodes.text: You stand and try the scene funny first. You use your face, hands, and voice to sell the joke. Then you do it again serious and quiet.

episodes.title: Missed Cue Moment
episodes.text: You are live and the other actor gives you your cue early. You blank on your next line for a second. The room goes quiet and waits.

choice.prompt: You missed your cue live. What do you do?

options.label: Stay in voice and pick up the line
options.outcome: You breathe, stay in character, and say your line late. The scene keeps moving and the others stay with you.

options.label: Pause and ask for the line
options.outcome: You stop and ask for help with the line. Someone feeds it to you and you start again from the cue.

episodes.title: Morning Walkthrough
episodes.text: You arrive as the plant hums low. You walk the basin deck and check each meter and gauge. Everything reads steady and you note the load for the morning.

episodes.title: First Samples
episodes.text: You pull on gloves and fill bottles at the inlet and the clear well. You run each through the test kit and match the color to the chart.

trial.title: Put testing in order
items: Match the color against the chart standard
Rinse the bottle and collect the water sample
Add the reagent and run the test equipment
Check the sample bottle is clean and labeled
trial.explain: You check the bottle first, then collect, test, and compare.

episodes.title: Adjusting The Flow
episodes.text: You stand at the control panel and watch the flow climb after the morning use. You rest your hand on the dial that steadies the clarifier feed.

choice.prompt: The inflow is rising. Do you adjust the controls now?

options.label: Open the feed a notch
options.outcome: You turn it up a little and watch the level settle back.

options.label: Leave it and watch longer
options.outcome: You stay at the panel and keep your eyes on the gauges.

episodes.title: Same Readings Again
episodes.text: You sit down with the same form as yesterday. You copy down meter and gauge readings line by line. You sign it and set it aside for tomorrow.

episodes.title: Pump Sounds Wrong
episodes.text: You hear a pump strain on your rounds and see one gauge reading low.

choice.prompt: The gauge is dropping and the pump is straining. What do you do?

options.label: Shut it down and inspect
options.outcome: You stop the pump and walk around it to look for the fault.

options.label: Keep it running and watch
options.outcome: You stay by the gauge and keep watching the pressure.

chat.text: That north pump sound off to you?
Shut that side down and check it before it trips?

episodes.title: Afternoon Chlorine Dose
episodes.text: You check the test result and wheel over the chlorine. You measure the dose and add it slow to the water. The smell fades as it mixes in.

episodes.title: Setting Up Rig
episodes.text: You arrive at the field and climb up to the controls. You work the levers to steady the machine on the ground. You shift the drill to position it and line it up over the mark.

choice.prompt: The rig still rocks a little as you line up the drill. Do you steady it again now?

options.label: Reset and steady again
options.outcome: You back off and steady the machine again. The drill lines up straight and holds still.

options.label: Keep the current setup
options.outcome: You stay with the setup and start slow. You watch it wobble and have to stop to steady it anyway.

episodes.title: Building Well Casing
episodes.text: You sit down at the work area with lengths of casing. You cut and fit them to size for the hole. You check the joints by hand before staging them nearby.

episodes.title: Holding Drill Speed
episodes.text: You sit at the controls and start the drill, then stop it, then start it again. You hold the same drilling speed for a long stretch. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Cooling the Bit
episodes.text: You pour water into the well as the drill turns. You watch the water carry the loose drillings back up. You keep the flow going to keep the bit cool.

trial.title: Hot Bit Check
trial.scenario: The bit is running hot and drillings are packing tight in the hole. The cuttings are not coming up clear.
options: Pour water to cool the bit and flush drillings
Push harder without water
Leave the bit dry and keep speed
trial.explain: Water cools the bit and washes drillings out of the hole.

episodes.title: Hard Rock Hit
episodes.text: You hit hard rock and the drill starts to strain.

choice.prompt: The rock is harder now and the drill is laboring. What do you change?

options.label: Ease off and reset air, rotary and pressure for hard rock
options.outcome: You lower the settings to match the hard rock. The drill steadies and cuts without binding.

options.label: Keep the same settings and push through
options.outcome: You hold the same pressure and speed. The bit heats up and the drill shakes harder until you have to stop.

chat.text: That sound changed. What kind of rock are you in?
Watch your air and rotary. What are you changing?

episodes.title: Setting the Casing
episodes.text: You slow the machine and stop the drill. You guide the casing you made into the hole. You control the speed as it slides down into place.

episodes.title: The core work
episodes.text: You start the main work of a Web Designer — the core of the job, done properly, start to finish. No audience and no shortcut: this is the thing everything else in the day supports. This is the work the whole job is built around.

episodes.title: People time
episodes.text: People need things from you — questions, help, decisions. You deal with them one at a time, the way this job always does. Real people, real reactions — this is the human side of the job, as it actually feels.

choice.prompt: Someone you're working with asks you to take on one more thing — extra work, on top of everything already in front of you today.

options.label: Say yes and fit it in
options.outcome: You fit it in. The day runs longer, the work gets done properly — and the person who asked remembers that you said yes.

options.label: Say no, politely
options.outcome: You say no, and you say why. A short, slightly awkward moment — then the rest of your day stays yours.

options.label: Offer a smaller version
options.outcome: You offer the part you can actually do, and by when. Most days that's accepted — saying yes to everything is how this job burns people out.

episodes.title: Hands on
episodes.text: Tools-and-systems time: you work the equipment and the screens of the trade until the thing in front of you does what it should. Skilled, hands-on work — the part where being good at it shows.

trial.title: The check-in
trial.says: Hey — how's that thing coming along that you were working on?
options: It's on track. I'll flag it straight away if I need help or it slips.
Fine.
Honestly? Don't ask. It's a disaster.
trial.explain: The professional reply says where things stand and what happens next — short, honest, no drama.

episodes.title: The routine block
episodes.text: The same block as yesterday: the repeating tasks that never make the brochure. You do them again, carefully, because skipping them is exactly how mistakes happen. The same again tomorrow. This block repeats more than any other part of the job.

episodes.title: It goes wrong
episodes.text: Something goes wrong — it always does, some days. A problem lands on you that was in nobody's plan, and sorting it out is now your job. Unplanned and unavoidable — how the job feels when it pushes back.

episodes.title: The paperwork
episodes.text: End of day: notes, records, the write-up of everything you did. The work isn't finished until it's written down. Nobody's favourite part. It still has to be done, every day.

episodes.title: Morning Venue Walk
episodes.text: You arrive at the venue with the couple. You walk the garden and the hall together. You point out where the light falls and agree what group shots you want.

episodes.title: Setting Up Gear
episodes.text: You sit down by your bag in the side room. You mount your digital camera on the tripod. You fit a filter and clip on the flash attachment.

episodes.title: Checking Camera Settings
episodes.text: You sit through the speeches and check focus again. You adjust aperture and shutter speed for the same indoor light. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Holding The Reflector
episodes.text: You stand in the courtyard for couple portraits and the sun keeps shifting.

choice.prompt: The light is harsh and they are squinting. What do you adjust first?

options.label: Move them and reset the reflector
options.outcome: You move them into open shade and angle the reflector. The harsh shadows lift and you start shooting again.

options.label: Keep shooting as is
options.outcome: You keep shooting in the hard sun. They keep squinting and the faces stay half in shadow.

chat.text: The sun is right in our eyes here.
I can hold the reflector if you want it bounced.
Can we move a little into the shade?

episodes.title: Losing The Light
episodes.text: You line up the first dance and the room goes dark. Your flash does not fire. The couple keeps moving across the floor.

choice.prompt: The flash is dead mid-dance. What do you do?

options.label: Swap to wider aperture and higher shutter care
options.outcome: You open the aperture and steady your focus for the low light. You keep shooting soft but usable frames until the flash is back.

options.label: Stop and fix the flash now
options.outcome: You step back to check the flash attachment. You miss the start of the dance while you work.

options.label: Add a second flash from your bag
options.outcome: You pull your backup flash and create artificial light from the side. You pick up the dance a few seconds later.

episodes.title: Backing Up Photos
episodes.text: You get home and sit at your desk. You plug in the cards and transfer the day's photographs to the computer.

trial.title: Save the day's work
items: Send the files for electronic transmission
Archive the edited files for storage
Transfer photographs to the computer
Edit the photographs on the computer
trial.explain: You move the files first, then edit and archive before you send anything.

episodes.title: Morning Couple Talk
episodes.text: You arrive at the cafe and open your notebook. You sit down with the couple to talk through what they want. You ask about their plans and write down their needs for the wedding.

choice.prompt: They want a late outdoor dinner but rain is likely. What do you ask them to decide now?

options.label: Pick an indoor backup plan now
options.outcome: You write down the indoor room as backup. The site staff holds it for the date.

options.label: Wait and decide next week
options.outcome: You note to revisit it next week. You keep the current outdoor plan for now.

episodes.title: Venue Walk Through
episodes.text: You walk the hall with the site staff. You check the entrances and where tables will go. You talk through the setup details together.

trial.title: Confirm site details
trial.says: We can only let vendors in after 4. Will that work for your setup?
options: Yes, I will tell catering and the other vendors to plan for entry after 4.
Just let them in whenever, it will be fine.
I do not handle vendor times.
trial.explain: You confirm the detail with site staff and pass it to vendors.

episodes.title: Food and Beds Booked
episodes.text: You sit at your desk and call catering and the hotel. You arrange rooms for out-of-town guests and confirm the meal count. You also book cars to move everyone between sites.

episodes.title: Checking the Bills
episodes.text: You open the catering and rental bills at your desk. You compare each line to what was ordered. You approve the correct ones for payment.

episodes.title: Same Vans Again
episodes.text: You sit at your desk and call the same van company. You confirm the same pickup times as yesterday. You log it the same way for tomorrow.

episodes.title: Missing Speakers Rush
episodes.text: You reach the hall and the speakers are not set up. Your phone buzzes with messages from the venue.

choice.prompt: The audio gear is missing and time is short. What do you do?

options.label: Call the backup audio supplier now
options.outcome: You call and book the spare speakers. They arrive and set up before guests sit down.

options.label: Keep calling the first company
options.outcome: You stay on the phone with them. You wait for their driver to confirm a new time.

options.label: Ask venue staff for spare gear
options.outcome: You ask the venue staff what they have on site. They bring out their small house system.

chat.text: The audio gear never arrived. Ceremony starts in an hour.
Rental company is not answering. What should we do?

episodes.title: Gear Up First
episodes.text: You arrive at the shop and pull on your helmet, gloves, and jacket. You check your ventilation and clear your area before you start. You run through your safe habits the same way every morning.

episodes.title: Straightedge And Template
episodes.text: You pick up the first workpieces and look them over for cracks and flaws. You lay a straightedge and template against each one to check the shape.

trial.title: Spot the defect
trial.scenario: You hold the straightedge flat against a workpiece. Light shows through under one edge and the template does not sit flush. The surface looks bent.
options: The workpiece is warped and out of spec
The straightedge is working normally
The template confirms the piece is fine
trial.explain: A gap under the straightedge means the piece does not match the specification.

episodes.title: Measuring Gaps Again
episodes.text: You sit with the calipers and micrometer and check grooves, angles, and gaps. You write down the numbers and move to the next joint. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Flat Weld Run
episodes.text: You clamp a component flat on the table and lower your hood. You run the bead steady across the joint and watch the puddle tie in. You lift your hood to check your work.

choice.prompt: The edges look close but the gap is a little tight. What do you do?

options.label: Weld it as set
options.outcome: You weld the joint as it is. The bead sits high and you have to grind and re-weld part of it.

options.label: Stop and re-check the gap
options.outcome: You stop and measure the gap again with calipers. You reset the parts and then make the weld.

episodes.title: Torch Sputters Out
episodes.text: You start a vertical weld and the arc stutters and dies. You stop and check the machine and the wire feed.

choice.prompt: The equipment keeps cutting out. What do you do?

options.label: Keep trying to weld through it
options.outcome: You keep striking the arc. The welds come out uneven and the machine keeps cutting out.

options.label: Stop and tell your supervisor
options.outcome: You shut off the machine and tell your supervisor what happened. The machine stays off until it is checked.

options.label: Switch to a different workpiece
options.outcome: You set this piece aside and try another one. The machine still faults on the new piece.

chat.text: That sputter sounded bad. Is your feeder jamming again?
Stop welding if the machine is acting up. What do you see?
Okay, leave the torch down. I will come look at it now.

episodes.title: Flagging Bad Stock
episodes.text: You find two pieces with pitted edges that will not clean up. You set them aside and walk them over to your supervisor. You show where the material is defective.

episodes.title: Morning Floor Walk
episodes.text: You arrive before anyone else and walk the floor with your checklist. You check the mats, the weights, and the locker rooms. Same list as yesterday, same again tomorrow.

episodes.title: Team Check In
episodes.text: You gather the fitness instructors and the nutritionist for the day's plan.

chat.text: Morning. My 10 AM is out sick, can you cover her stretch class?
I have three nutrition consults back to back. Do I have time for notes between them?
Remember to confirm who is closing the weight room tonight.

episodes.title: Building a Plan
episodes.text: You sit down with a new member to coordinate her weekly fitness program. You look at her schedule and the classes you have open. You talk through what fits her mornings.

choice.prompt: She can only come twice a week. What do you put in her plan?

options.label: Fill it with two full-body fitness sessions
options.outcome: She books both sessions and you add them to the schedule. You note to check how she feels next week.

options.label: Add a third home session she can do alone
options.outcome: You write out the home session and add it to her service plan. She takes the paper and says she will try it.

episodes.title: Torn Cable
episodes.text: You are crossing the weight room when you see a cable machine with a frayed cable. A member is standing nearby waiting to use it. The area is not safe right now.

choice.prompt: The cable is frayed and someone wants to use it. What do you do first?

options.label: Close the machine now and tag it out of use
options.outcome: You block the machine and put up the out-of-use tag. You log the fault so it gets fixed.

options.label: Let him do one quick set, then close it
options.outcome: You stay with the machine while he finishes. You close it right after and log the damage.

episodes.title: New Class Ideas
episodes.text: You sit at your desk to review two new service ideas for next month. You compare their cost and how many members they might serve. You need to recommend one to keep costs down.

trial.title: Pick the safer offer
trial.scenario: You have two proposals. One is a low-cost morning stretch service using your clean studio and current staff. The other needs costly new equipment and extra staff you do not have.
options: The low-cost stretch service using current staff
The costly new service needing new gear
Offer both even though staff and money are short
trial.explain: The low-cost option fits your staff, space, and budget.

episodes.title: Logs and Reports
episodes.text: You return to your desk to update the schedules and daily records. You enter attendance, staff hours, and the broken cable report. You save the file and close out the day.

episodes.title: Morning Restart Check
episodes.text: You arrive at the base of the turbine as the sun comes up. You climb up and sit down at the control panel. You start the turbine generator system and watch it come up to speed to make sure it runs right.

episodes.title: Same Bolts Again
episodes.text: You walk your row for routine maintenance on the turbine equipment. You check the same covers, fasteners, and cable runs as yesterday. You log nothing new. Same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Testing The Converter
episodes.text: You open the converter cabinet and set out your meter. You test the electrical components with your multimeter and infrared tester. You write down each reading as you go.

trial.title: Pick what to check
trial.scenario: You are testing electrical parts in the converter system with a multimeter and infrared tester. One breaker reads normal voltage and normal heat. One wire shows low voltage and a hot spot.
options: The normal breaker
The low-voltage hot wire
The cabinet door latch
trial.explain: You check the low-voltage hot wire first because it shows the fault.

episodes.title: Talking Through Pitch Fault
episodes.text: You stand at the pitch system cabinet with your colleague after lunch.

choice.prompt: The variable pitch fault is back. What do you check first?

options.label: Check the hydraulic lines and fittings
options.outcome: You find a damp fitting and tighten it. You wipe it clean and watch for fresh leaks.

options.label: Reset the pitch control and watch
options.outcome: You reset the pitch control. The fault clears, then comes back after one pitch cycle.

chat.text: Pitch fault is back on number two blade. You seeing it too?
Hydraulic pressure looks low on my screen. Want to open it up?
Tell me what you want to check first.

episodes.title: Generator Stops Hard
episodes.text: You are at the controls when the wind turbine generator trips and stops. The control system shows a fault and will not clear. You need to diagnose the generator and control system problem now.

choice.prompt: The generator is down with a control fault. What do you do?

options.label: Run diagnosis on the control system first
options.outcome: You step through the controller alarms. You find a speed control fault holding the start.

options.label: Inspect the generator and converter wiring
options.outcome: You open the panels and look over the generator leads. You see no burn marks and go back to the alarms.

options.label: Call for a shutdown and lock out
options.outcome: You lock out the system and tag it. The turbine stays stopped until the fault is cleared.

episodes.title: Second Start Attempt
episodes.text: You stand back at the control panel after the repair. You press through the restart sequence for the turbine generator system. You stay and watch the speed hold steady to make sure the operation is proper.

episodes.title: Sweeping the Lobby
episodes.text: You arrive before the doors open. You sweep the lobby floor and push the dust into a pile. You vacuum the mats by the entrance.

episodes.title: Restrooms Need Attention
episodes.text: You start your restroom round on the first floor. A worker waits outside while you clean and restock. You wipe the sinks and refill the soap and paper.

choice.prompt: One stall is still occupied and people are waiting. What do you do now?

options.label: Clean the open area now, then come back
options.outcome: You finish the sinks and trash and return in ten minutes to finish the stall. The line moves and the restroom gets fully cleaned.

options.label: Wait outside until it is fully free
options.outcome: You stand by with your cart until the room clears. You then clean everything at once before moving on.

episodes.title: Emptying Every Bin
episodes.text: You walk the same hallway with the same trash bag. You gather and empty every small bin into the big bag. You tie it off and drop in a fresh liner. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Mopping the Hallway
episodes.text: You sweep the back hallway first. You mop the sticky spots and scrub the corner by the door. You let the floor dry before you move the sign.

episodes.title: Water Under the Sink
episodes.text: You find water spreading under the restroom sink. You message your manager about the need for a major repair.

choice.prompt: Water is still spreading on the floor. What do you do first?

options.label: Notify the manager now and stand by
options.outcome: You send the message with the location and stay by the leak. Maintenance arrives knowing exactly where to go.

options.label: Mop it up first, then notify
options.outcome: You mop the standing water and then message the manager. The leak keeps dripping until maintenance is called.

chat.text: That water is getting to the wall fast.
Can you shut the valve and stay there?
I am calling maintenance for a major repair.

episodes.title: Locking Up Late
episodes.text: You check the appliances are off so no hazards are left. You walk the empty floor and check the restrooms. You lock the doors after hours and test the handle.

trial.title: Final safety check
trial.scenario: You do your last walk after hours. One break room appliance is still hot and two doors are already locked.
options: Coffee warmer left on in the break room
Locked door on the first floor
Emptied trash bin in the lobby
trial.explain: A hot appliance left on can create a hazard overnight.

episodes.title: The core work
episodes.text: You start the main work of a Winemaker / Enologist — the core of the job, done properly, start to finish. No audience and no shortcut: this is the thing everything else in the day supports. This is the work the whole job is built around.

episodes.title: People time
episodes.text: People need things from you — questions, help, decisions. You deal with them one at a time, the way this job always does. Real people, real reactions — this is the human side of the job, as it actually feels.

choice.prompt: Someone you're working with asks you to take on one more thing — extra work, on top of everything already in front of you today.

options.label: Say yes and fit it in
options.outcome: You fit it in. The day runs longer, the work gets done properly — and the person who asked remembers that you said yes.

options.label: Say no, politely
options.outcome: You say no, and you say why. A short, slightly awkward moment — then the rest of your day stays yours.

options.label: Offer a smaller version
options.outcome: You offer the part you can actually do, and by when. Most days that's accepted — saying yes to everything is how this job burns people out.

episodes.title: Hands on
episodes.text: Hands-on time. You make, fix or adjust the real thing in front of you — the part of the job you can touch, and the part where skill is visible. Skilled, hands-on work — the part where being good at it shows.

trial.title: The check-in
trial.says: Hey — how's that thing coming along that you were working on?
options: It's on track. I'll flag it straight away if I need help or it slips.
Fine.
Honestly? Don't ask. It's a disaster.
trial.explain: The professional reply says where things stand and what happens next — short, honest, no drama.

episodes.title: The routine block
episodes.text: The same block as yesterday: the repeating tasks that never make the brochure. You do them again, carefully, because skipping them is exactly how mistakes happen. The same again tomorrow. This block repeats more than any other part of the job.

episodes.title: It goes wrong
episodes.text: Something goes wrong — it always does, some days. A problem lands on you that was in nobody's plan, and sorting it out is now your job. Unplanned and unavoidable — how the job feels when it pushes back.

episodes.title: The paperwork
episodes.text: End of day: notes, records, the write-up of everything you did. The work isn't finished until it's written down. Nobody's favourite part. It still has to be done, every day.

episodes.title: Planning Morning Routines
episodes.text: You arrive before anyone else and sit on the floor with your notebook. You check today's list for capabilities and limitations. You pick movements for each muscle set and choose music to match.

trial.title: Put the routine together
items: Pick music to match the pace
Check what the group can and can't do
Lay out the order of the routine
Pick a movement for each muscle set
trial.explain: You check limits first, then pick movements and order before music.

episodes.title: Meeting New Student
episodes.text: You sit down with a new participant before class. You ask about injuries, needs, and what feels hard. You note a knee issue and plan a gentler starting program.

episodes.title: Watching The Row
episodes.text: You walk the row during standing poses and watch form.

choice.prompt: Her knee is caving in and she looks unsure. What do you do now?

options.label: Give a short correction now
options.outcome: You tell her to shift weight and straighten the knee. She adjusts and holds the pose steadier.

options.label: Offer a supported alternative
options.outcome: You show her the chair version of the pose. She follows it and finishes the set without strain.

chat.text: My balance feels off on this side.
You notice her knee is caving in.

episodes.title: Midday Gentle Class
episodes.text: You lead the same midday sequence as yesterday. You call the same cues and offer the same easier versions. Tomorrow will be the same again.

episodes.title: Checking Regular Progress
episodes.text: You watch two regulars move through their sets. You see one has more strength than last month. You write a note to add a harder progression next week.

episodes.title: When Movement Hurts
episodes.text: Halfway through class a participant stops and holds his shoulder. He says the overhead reach does not feel right. You step closer to check.

choice.prompt: He cannot do the overhead reach without pain. What do you do?

options.label: Swap his movement now
options.outcome: You give him a low chest-level alternative and he rejoins the set. You note to adapt his program after class.

options.label: Pause him and watch
options.outcome: You have him rest and breathe while others finish. You talk with him after about changing his plan.

options.label: Adjust the whole set
options.outcome: You switch the class to a gentler shoulder movement. Everyone follows along and he stays comfortable.
